title_en: FAA orders checks on nearly 2,000 Boeing 737s after pitch oscillation events
title_zh: 俯仰振荡事件发生后，FAA 下令对近 2,000 架波音 737 进行检查
summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered inspections of nearly 2,000 Boeing 737 Next Generation aircraft after… The post FAA orders checks on nearly 2,000 Boeing 737s after pitch oscillation events appeared first on AeroTime .
summary_zh: 美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 已下令对近 2,000 架下一代波音 737 飞机进行检查……
body_en: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered inspections of nearly 2,000 Boeing 737 Next Generation aircraft after multiple operators reported pitch oscillations linked to excessive looseness in the horizontal stabilizer mechanism.

The airworthiness directive, published on October 19, 2026, requires operators to measure movement in the stabilizer’s pivot hinges and jackscrew, then carry out additional checks, repairs or parts replacements depending on the findings.
The FAA estimates that 1,987 US-registered aircraft are affected. The directive covers 737-600, -700, -700C, -800, -900 and -900ER aircraft. It does not apply to the 737 MAX.
The rule takes effect on November 23, 2026, with inspections due according to the compliance schedule incorporated into the directive.

The horizontal stabilizer is the movable horizontal surface on the aircraft’s tail that helps control its nose-up or nose-down attitude. Excessive movement within its supporting mechanism, known as freeplay, can allow unwanted motion.

The FAA said the reported pitch oscillations were caused by excessive stabilizer freeplay and warned that leaving the condition uncorrected could lead to flutter, a potentially dangerous vibration that can result in loss of control.
The final directive follows a proposed rule published in January 2026 and incorporates inspection procedures detailed in a Boeing bulletin from June 12, 2025.
body_zh: 在多家运营商报告水平安定面机构过度松动导致俯仰振荡后，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 已下令对近 2,000 架下一代波音 737 飞机进行检查。
2026 年 10 月 19 日发布的适航指令要求运营商测量稳定器枢轴铰链和螺旋千斤顶的运动，然后根据结果进行额外的检查、维修或零件更换。

该规则于 2026 年 11 月 23 日生效，并根据指令中纳入的合规时间表进行检查。

Atlanta City Council has ratified Delta Air Lines' $12 million takeover of two former Spirit Airlines gates at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL). The decision, made Monday, covers gates C4 and C6 in Concourse C, along with ticketing and support space vacated after Spirit stopped flying in May.

The agreement further strengthens Delta's position at the world's busiest airport, where it already dominates passenger traffic and flight operations . It also fits into a broader redistribution of Spirit's airport assets, from Chicago and New York to Las Vegas and Fort Lauderdale.
Delta Pays $12 Million For Spirit's Atlanta Airport Gates

The council approved Resolution 26-R-4262 by 15 votes to zero, authorizing the city's acknowledgment of the lease assignment. Atlanta News & Talk Radio WSB reported that Delta is acquiring preferential-use rights, not ownership of the gates themselves, in an agreement that runs until June 30. The two gates are located in Concourse C, the central of ATL's seven concourses, where Delta already operates 19 gates.

title_en: Delta Ran Icelandair Out Of Detroit, Then Cut The Route Itself: The Nasty Side Of Competition
title_zh: 达美航空将冰岛航空从底特律撤出，然后又自行削减航线：竞争的令人讨厌的一面
summary: Icelandair launched Detroit to Keflavik in 2023, Delta matched it, Icelandair left, and now Delta has cut the route too. Detroit is back to zero Iceland flights.
summary_zh: 冰岛航空于2023年开通了底特律飞往凯夫拉维克的航线，达美航空也跟进了，冰岛航空离开了，现在达美航空也削减了这条航线。底特律回到零 Icela
body_en: Usually we say that competition is good for consumers, but here’s a case where it isn’t, as a Delta hub will go from having two airlines flying to Iceland, to having zero airlines flying to Iceland. I guess there’s no one to really blame here, but it’s bad for consumers!
Delta cuts Detroit to Keflavik route, after Icelandair exit

Icelandair operates a unique business model, whereby it uses its hub in Keflavik (KEF) to serve markets on both sides of the Atlantic, so that the airline can tap into the local market, as well as offer one-stop service all over the place.

In 2023, we saw Icelandair launch flights to Detroit (DTW) . Detroit is a fortress hub for Delta, so the airline has a lot of pricing power there. Of course Icelandair’s idea was to undercut the major players on pricing, while also giving travelers the opportunity of a stopover in Iceland.

As you’d expect, airlines tend to defend their hubs, so less than two weeks after Icelandair’s announcement, Delta announced it would launch exactly the same route , and would even start the service three days earlier. This was obviously not a coincidence, but a competitive response.

Admittedly I suspect Icelandair had to know that Delta might replicate its route, and that proved to be too much competition. In early 2026, Icelandair fully ended Detroit service, as it couldn’t make the math work. Well, at least consumers would still have one option to Iceland, right? Not so fast, unfortunately.
body_zh: 通常我们说竞争对消费者有利，但这里的情况却并非如此，因为达美航空枢纽将从拥有两家飞往冰岛的航空公司变成拥有零家飞往冰岛的航空公司。我想这并不能怪罪任何人，但这对消费者来说是不利的！
冰岛航空退出后，达美航空削减了底特律至凯夫拉维克的航线
冰岛航空采用独特的商业模式，利用凯夫拉维克枢纽（KEF）服务大西洋两岸市场，既能开拓当地市场，又能提供遍布各地的一站式服务。
2023 年，冰岛航空开通了飞往底特律 (DTW) 的航班。底特律是达美航空的要塞枢纽，因此该航空公司在那里拥有很大的定价权。当然，冰岛航空的想法是在价格上低于主要参与者，同时也为旅行者提供在冰岛中途停留的机会。
正如你所料，航空公司倾向于保卫自己的枢纽，因此在冰岛航空宣布这一消息后不到两周，达美航空就宣布将推出完全相同的航线，甚至提前三天开始服务。这显然不是巧合，而是一种竞争反应。

body_en: Few aircraft have maintained their status as foundational long-haul workhorses quite like the Boeing 777 family. The iconic widebody revolutionized global connectivity with its twin-engine efficiency, spacious cabin design, and unmatched operational reliability. Newer generations of composite aircraft like the Boeing 787 and Airbus A350 gradually dominate delivery schedules, but a select group of global carriers continues to rely on the pioneer variants of this legendary lineage. title_en: Lufthansa Loses Greenwashing Lawsuit, Rebrands Green Fares As Impact Fares
title_zh: 汉莎航空败诉绿色清洗诉讼，将绿色票价重新命名为影响力票价
summary: Lufthansa is renaming its Green Fares to Impact Fares after losing a greenwashing lawsuit brought by Environmental Action Germany. Here's what's changing and what stays the same.
summary_zh: 在德国环境行动组织提起的绿色清洗诉讼败诉后，汉莎航空将其绿色票价更名为影响票价。这是变化的
body_en: In 2023, Lufthansa introduced “Green Fares.” As you may have guessed based on the name, the idea is that these fares offer some level of carbon offsets, but beyond that, they offer added flexibility, plus bonus miles and status qualification. Well, Lufthansa has now announced that it’s rebranding these fares , and the change isn’t voluntary…
Lufthansa Group is renaming its Green Fares, and going forward, they’ll be known as Impact Fares. Here’s how Lufthansa describes this change:

The Lufthansa Group is renaming its Green Fare to Impact Fare. The new name places even stronger emphasis on customers’ contribution to greater sustainability in aviation and thus reflects new regulatory requirements for environmental communication: By choosing an Impact Fare, passengers support the additional use of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) across the Lufthansa Group’s route network. In addition, they contribute to selected climate protection projects outside the company’s value chain.

Lufthansa explains that for every Impact Fare booked, the company deploys an additional amount of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) in its flight operation within six months of departure. For flights within Europe, this volume is based on 20% of the estimated flight related CO2 emissions.

body_en: In the United States, it’s common to find flight attendants of all ages. There’s no maximum age to work as a flight attendant, as long as you can pass your recurrent training each year. The system also greatly incentivizes sticking around when you’re senior, since you’re maxed out on pay, and get your choice of routes, given seniority based bidding.
Along those lines, American’s current most senior flight attendant is about to retire, and I think that makes for an interesting story.
83-year-old American flight attendant retires after 63+ years

Ted Reed has the story of how American Airlines’ most senior flight attendant, Carol Fair, will be retiring on Monday, October 26, 2026, as she takes her last flight from London (LHR) to Charlotte (CLT). The 83-year-old first started her career in 1963 at Piedmont Airlines, before working at US Airways, and then American (given all the mergers). So she’ll be retiring after a career of over 63 years.

Fair is retiring as the number one active flight attendant on American’s seniority list, which includes around 30,000 people. Technically she’s only the third most senior flight attendant at the airline, but the two most senior no longer fly, but haven’t officially retired. Funny enough, when Fair first started her career, she was rejected at American, as the airline claimed she “wasn’t American material.” However, two mergers later, she landed at the airline she hoped to work for in the first place.

I had a roughly four hour layover, as I had arrived in Philippine Airlines’ A330 business class from Osaka (KIX) , and was connecting to Philippine Airlines’ A350 business class to San Francisco (SFO).

On the plus side, I didn’t have to switch terminals this time around, because a terminal change in Manila makes for what’s possibly the world’s worst airport transit experience . However, that’s not to say that the layover was smooth — quite to the contrary, I found the entire ground experience to be pretty bad . Transit security was a mess, and the lounge was overcrowded, with some major shortcomings.

Some may think my review here is overly critical, but let me simply state that somehow the lounge Wi-Fi doesn’t work on “foreign” computers (based on my experience, and confirmed by an airline employee), and that’s just mind-boggling to me. So if you want to use Wi-Fi on your laptop, you actually have to leave the lounge and go into the terminal, and use the airport free Wi-Fi. That’s just beyond embarrassing. Anyway, enough of an intro, let me get into the review.

Fortunately my Philippine Airlines flights were both arriving at and departing from Terminal 1 in Manila, so at least I didn’t have to switch terminals. All international connecting passengers have to clear transit security, and I found this to be a mess.

summary_zh: 巴西制造商巴西航空工业公司 (Embraer) 在 2026 年第三季度全公司范围内的积压订单达到了创纪录的 357 亿美元……
body_en: Brazilian manufacturer Embraer has reached a record company-wide backlog of $35.7 billion during the third quarter of 2026, up 3% from the previous three months.
On October 23, 2026, Embraer declared that the third quarter had been marked by “strong commercial activity,” with sizeable firm orders for E-Jets from both Abra Group and ANA Holdings.
During the third quarter, with its commercial aviation sector, Embraer logged 36 firm orders and 30 purchase rights or options for its E2-family.
The company’s Executive Aviation division also posted a record-high $8.2 billion backlog, up 5% from the second quarter of 2026.
The period was notable for the launch of the Phenom 300EV and delivery of the first Praetor 600E to launch customer Flexjet.
In Defense and Security, the backlog reached $6.1 billion in the third quarter, a 56% increase from the same period in 2025.
Among the highlights, the Fuerza Aeroespacial Colombiana (FAC) ordered two KC-390 Millennium multi-mission aircraft in August 2026, worth around $366.4 million.
Embraer currently has 43 firm orders for KC-390 Millennium military transport, plus 25 for A-29 Super Tucano light attack aircraft.
With nine months of the year now having passed, Embraer has delivered 52 commercial aircraft. The company is aiming to deliver between 80 and 85 in total by the end of the year.
Overall, 115 executive aircraft have been delivered to customers so far this year. Embraer hopes to deliver between 160 and 170.
body_zh: 巴西制造商巴西航空工业公司 2026 年第三季度全公司未完成订单达到创纪录的 357 亿美元，较前三个月增长 3%。
2026 年 10 月 23 日，巴西航空工业公司宣布第三季度“商业活动强劲”，Abra 集团和全日空控股公司都获得了大量 E-Jets 订单。
第三季度，巴西航空工业公司在商用航空领域获得了 36 份确认订单以及 30 份 E2 系列购买权或选择权。
该公司的公务航空部门还公布了创纪录的 82 亿美元积压订单，较 2026 年第二季度增长 5%。
这段时期值得注意的是 Phenom 300EV 的推出以及为客户 Flexjet 交付的第一架 Praetor 600E。
在国防和安全领域，第三季度积压订单达到 61 亿美元，比 2025 年同期增长 56%。
其中亮点包括哥伦比亚航空航天公司 (FAC) 于 2026 年 8 月订购了两架 KC-390 Millennium 多任务飞机，价值约 3.664 亿美元。
巴西航空工业公司目前拥有 43 份 KC-390 Millennium 军用运输机确认订单，以及 25 份 A-29 超级巨嘴鸟轻型攻击机订单。

summary_zh: Autoflight V5000 矩阵 william.moore@…
body_en: The V5000 Matrix is a lift-plus-cruise hybrid-electric/all-electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft being developed by AutoFlight Europe GmbH. Unveiled in February 2026, the aircraft performed a remotely piloted transition from thrustborne hover to wingborne cruise, demonstrating that flight testing is already underway. Industry commentators have suggested that entry into service could be as soon as 2027/2028, although there is no confirmation of this. Certification is to be sought from the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) under powered-lift regulations. Structure and Powertrain The Matrix pushes regulations to their maximum, being a 10 seat eVTOL with a maximum take-off weight of 5,700kg (hybrid version). The aircraft could be configured in a 6-seat VIP layout, or a 9-seat business layout plus a pilot. It will also feature a lavatory, the first eVTOL design to incorporate this, an indication of its lengthier flight duration capabilities. An uncrewed cargo variant is also in development. The intended market is more regional-focused than previous eVTOL designs. Structurally, the V5000 is an evolution of the previous Autoflight Prosperity I and CarryAll cargo variant. It features a long, aerodynamic cabin with panoramic viewing windows and skid-style landing gear. A main high wing is complemented by two smaller wings to the front and rear of the aircraft, with three booms extending across all three wings parallel to the cabin, on each side. 20 two-blade fixed propellers are mounted to the six booms to provide lift, while eight cruise propellers provide forward thrust, four mounted to the front and four to the rear. title_en: Turkey Signs $11 Billion Eurofighter Deal
title_zh: 土耳其签署价值 110 亿美元的欧洲战斗机协议
summary: Turkey Signs $11 Billion Eurofighter Deal hockensmithawi… Mon, 10/27/2025 - 18:19 Turkey has signed a long-anticipated £8 billion ($11 billion) deal to acquire Eurofighter Typhoons, the first major export contract for the four-nation combat aircraft since 2017
summary_zh: 土耳其签署价值 110 亿美元的欧洲战斗机协议 hockensmithawi…
body_en: Turkey has signed a long-anticipated £8 billion ($11 billion) deal to acquire Eurofighter Typhoons, the first major export contract for the four-nation combat aircraft since 2017. Twenty new-built aircraft will be purchased in the country’s first acquisition of a European combat aircraft after decades of operating new and secondhand U.S.-built fighters. But Turkey’s Eurofighter order could more than double in size, according to Turkish Defense Minister Yasar Guler. He declared that Ankara would also buy another 24 aircraft second hand, 12 each from Oman and Qatar. If those sales go through, Oman would be giving up Eurofighter operations. With deliveries of the new-build aircraft not due until 2030, delivering those second-hand aircraft—potentially as early as next year from Qatar, according to Guler—would allow Turkey to accelerate the Eurofighter’s entry into service and enable the retirement of older aircraft from its inventory, including the McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom. BAE Systems, which will produce the newly built aircraft in Warton, England, says it will receive £5.4 billion of the £8 billion deal. Included in the £5.4 billion are the aircraft and the weapons package from MBDA, including some integration work, potentially for Turkish indigenous weaponry. The remaining £2.6 billion is support and training activity, which will be contracted later, BAE Systems officials say. It is unclear whether the deal will ultimately include offsets to enable Turkish industry to become involved in the Eurofighter program and for Turkey to have a level of freedom of action for the fleet. After decades of facing numerous arms embargoes, Turkey often demands the ability to locally perform airframe, system and engine maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) in-country. The deal was struck during a meeting between UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Ankara. Starmer said the deal was a win for British workers and the wider UK defense industry. Government officials claim the order is “saving the Warton production line,” after concerns about a lack of new orders for UK-built Typhoons were expressed by workers unions. UK industry has a 37% share in the Eurofighter program and production of major component assemblies is being ramped up thanks to orders from the other Eurofighter partner nations including Germany, Italy and Spain. “Today’s announcement extends Typhoon production and preserves crucial sovereign skills which underpin the UK’s defense and security,” BAE Systems CEO Charles Woodburn said. The deal is another major boost for the UK defense industry, coming just weeks after the UK’s Type 26 frigates were selected by Norway in a £10 billion deal. UK Defense Secretary John Healey said the deal went beyond the procurement of aircraft. “It is the leading edge of the growing defense and industrial partnership between our two nations,” he said. As part of the visit, Starmer also visited the facilities of Turkish Aerospace Industries, where he was shown the indigenous Kaan combat aircraft. He was also exposed to the Hurjet advanced jet trainer, a potential candidate to replace the BAE Systems Hawk jet trainer in the UK Royal Air Force (RAF) inventory. The deal follows three years of negotiations, which have included lobbying of the German government for Berlin to lift a restriction on a Eurofighter sale after Erdoğan’s government arrested Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu, who is seen as a serious presidential rival to Erdoğan in upcoming elections. The administration of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz lifted the sanctions in part because of the benefit to German industry. A memorandum of understanding between the UK and Turkish governments for a Eurofighter sale was agreed to in July. Turkey’s interest in the aircraft is driven in part by a need for a more capable air combat platform to be available in the interim until advanced versions of the Kaan aircraft are produced in the 2030s. Ankara’s decision to opt for a European fighter, meanwhile, will have been driven by a need to diversify sources of supply after facing sanctions from the U.S. over its purchase of a Russian air defense system and banishment from the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter program. The transfer of Omani and Qatari aircraft to Turkey begs questions over the future of additional Eurofighter orders from Qatar, which has long been linked to orders for a further 12 aircraft for a total of 36. Oman, meanwhile, appears to want to consolidate its fighter fleet around the Lockheed Martin F-16 Block 50. In BAE Systems’ 2023 full-year results, the company revealed that the Omani air force had chosen not to renew support arrangements for its Typhoons, and it is unclear how active that fleet now is. Buying these additional aircraft would mean Turkey would have a mix of three configurations in its fleet. Qatar’s aircraft have the Mk.0 version of the active electronically scanned array European Common Radar System (ECRS) radar, while Oman’s feature the mechanically scanned Captor sensor. In addition to the Eurofighter order, Erdoğan and Starmer also revealed they were working on a new trade and security pact.

title_en: Second B-21 Enters Flight Test In Palmdale

summary: Second B-21 Enters Flight Test In Palmdale hockensmithawi… Thu, 09/11/2025 - 18:36 The B-21 Raider program completed the first flight of a second airborne test aircraft in Palmdale, California on Sept. 11, clearing a key milestone a month before the 10th anniv
summary_zh: 第二架 B-21 在棕榈谷进行飞行测试 hockensmithawi…
body_en: The B-21 Raider program completed the first flight of a second airborne test aircraft in Palmdale, California on Sept. 11, clearing a key milestone a month before the 10th anniversary of the U.S. Air Force contract award to Northrop Grumman. Witnesses posted video on social media showing the B-21 flight-test aircraft passing overhead with wheels retracted and followed by a Lockheed Martin F-16 chase plane. “We can now expedite critical evaluations of mission systems and weapons capabilities, directly supporting the strategic deterrence and combat effectiveness envisioned for this aircraft,” Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said. Northrop assembles all B-21s inside Building 401 on Site 4 of the Air Force’s Plant 42 complex at Palmdale Regional Airport. New test aircraft must fly out of the public airport after they have been assembled, before they can relocate to the secure area of nearby Edwards Air Force Base. The milestone comes nearly 22 months after Northrop completed the maiden sortie of the first flight test version of the B-21 on Nov. 10, 2023. The company has also delivered to the Air Force two more fully assembled airframes, which are reserved for static and fatigue testing on the ground. Two more flight-test aircraft have been in some stage of assembly since at least February 2022. Air Force officials say the program remains on track to clear the initial operational capability milestone in the mid-2020s. Northrop won the $21.4 billion contract in October 2015 for the engineering and manufacturing development phase of the Long-Range Strike Bomber, which the Air Force later rechristened as the B-21 Raider. The Air Force also signed orders with Northrop for the first two-year lots of low-rate initial production.
body_zh: B-21 Raider 项目于 9 月 11 日在加利福尼亚州帕姆代尔完成了第二架机载测试机的首飞，在美国空军授予诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司合同 10 周年前一个月实现了一个重要的里程碑。目击者在社交媒体上发布的视频显示，轮子收起的 B-21 试飞机从头顶飞过，后面跟着一架洛克希德·马丁公司的 F-16 追击机。空军部长特洛伊·梅克说：“我们现在可以加快对任务系统和武器能力的关键评估，直接支持这架飞机的战略威慑和战斗力。”诺斯罗普公司在帕姆代尔地区机场空军 42 号工厂 4 号基地的 401 号楼内组装所有 B-21。新的测试飞机必须在组装后飞离公共机场，然后才能转移到附近爱德华兹空军基地的安全区域。这一里程碑是在诺斯罗普公司于 2023 年 11 月 10 日完成 B-21 首次飞行测试版本的首次飞行近 22 个月后实现的。该公司还向空军交付了两架组装更齐全的机身，用于地面静态和疲劳测试。至少自 2022 年 2 月起，另外两架飞行测试飞机已进入组装阶段。空军官员表示，该计划仍在按计划进行，将在 2020 年代中期实现初始作战能力里程碑。诺斯罗普公司于 2015 年 10 月赢得了价值 214 亿美元的合同，用于远程攻击轰炸机的工程和制造开发阶段，空军后来将其重新命名为 B-21 袭击者。空军还与诺斯罗普公司签署了前两年批量低速初始生产的订单。
